# k3ctx — LLM/Agent Usage Guide

k3ctx manages SSH tunnels and kubectl contexts for K3s clusters.
All commands are flag-driven. No interactive input is required.

---

## Invocation

    k3ctx <command> [flags]

JSON output is automatic when stdout is not a terminal (pipe, redirect, agent).
Force JSON explicitly: k3ctx <command> --json

---

## Output format

Success:
    {"ok": true, "command": "<name>", "data": {...}}

Error:
    {"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "hint": "..."}}

Errors go to stdout as JSON (not stderr) when in JSON mode.
Log/debug messages always go to stderr and never appear in JSON output.

---

## Exit codes

    0  success
    1  general error or missing required --yes flag
    2  connection failed (SSH or API unreachable)
    3  ambiguous match — multiple hosts matched the query
    4  no match — no hosts found for the query

---

## Commands

### init
Initialize local config and storage directories.

    k3ctx init

Output: {"ok": true, "command": "init", "data": {"initialized": true}}

---

### clients [query]
List clients with host counts. Supports pagination.

    k3ctx clients [query] [--limit N] [--cursor TOKEN] [--refresh-inventory]

Flags:
  --limit N           Max results per page (default 20)
  --cursor TOKEN      Pagination cursor from previous response
  --refresh-inventory Run git pull on inventory before listing

Output data:
    {
      "items": [{"client": "acme", "host_count": 3}],
      "page":  {"limit": 20, "returned": 3, "total": 3, "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null}
    }

Pagination: if has_more=true, pass next_cursor value as --cursor in the next call.

---

### hosts CLIENT [query]
List or search hosts in one client. Supports pagination.

    k3ctx hosts CLIENT [query] [--host NAME] [--id SF_ID] [--ip ADDR]
                               [--limit N] [--cursor TOKEN] [--refresh-inventory]

Flags:
  --host NAME         Filter by host name (substring)
  --id SF_ID          Filter by systemframe_id
  --ip ADDR           Filter by IP address
  --limit N           Max results per page (default 20)
  --cursor TOKEN      Pagination cursor
  --refresh-inventory Run git pull on inventory before listing

Output data:
    {
      "items": [
        {"client": "acme", "host_name": "prod", "context_name": "acme-prod",
         "addr_ip": "10.0.0.10", "systemframe_id": "sf-123"}
      ],
      "page": {"limit": 20, "returned": 1, "total": 1, "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null}
    }

---

### connect [IDENTIFIERS...]
Resolve identifiers and connect to a cluster. Opens an SSH tunnel and merges
kubeconfig into ~/.kube/config.

    k3ctx connect [query] [--client C] [--host H] [--id ID] [--ip IP]
                          [--context CTX] [--refresh-inventory]

Flags:
  --client C          Filter by client name
  --host H            Filter by host name
  --id ID             Filter by systemframe_id
  --ip IP             Filter by IP address
  --context CTX       Exact context name (fastest, no ambiguity)
  --refresh-inventory Run git pull on inventory before connecting

Output data (ConnectResult):
    {
      "success": true,
      "context_name": "acme-prod",
      "local_port": 16443,
      "internal_ip": "10.0.0.10",
      "tunnel_pid": 12345,
      "used_cache": false,
      "argocd_local_port": 18080,
      "alertmanager_local_port": null,
      "victoriametrics_local_port": null,
      "network_requirement": {"type": null, "network_range": null, "needs_vpn": false},
      "error": null
    }

Exit codes:
  4  NO_MATCH         — no host matched the query
  3  AMBIGUOUS_MATCH  — multiple hosts matched; use --context to disambiguate
  1  TARGET_NOT_FOUND — could not load target from inventory
  2  CONNECTION_FAILED — SSH tunnel or API verification failed

---

### status
Show active contexts and their tunnel state.

    k3ctx status

Output data: array of context status objects
    [{"context_name": "acme-prod", "tunnel_running": true}]

---

### tunnel-list
List context names with running SSH tunnels.

    k3ctx tunnel-list

Output data: array of context name strings
    ["acme-prod", "acme-staging"]

---

### tunnel-kill CONTEXT
Kill one managed tunnel. DESTRUCTIVE — requires --yes.

    k3ctx tunnel-kill CONTEXT --yes

Without --yes: exit 1, code REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION.

---

### tunnel-kill-all
Kill all managed tunnels. DESTRUCTIVE — requires --yes.

    k3ctx tunnel-kill-all --yes

Without --yes: exit 1, code REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION.

---

## Error codes reference

    NO_MATCH              connect found no hosts matching the query
    AMBIGUOUS_MATCH       connect found multiple hosts; add filters
    TARGET_NOT_FOUND      matched context not found in inventory
    CONNECTION_FAILED     SSH or Kubernetes API connection failed
    REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION destructive command called without --yes
    COMMAND_ERROR         generic command or config error

---

## Destructive commands

These commands modify system state and require --yes:

    tunnel-kill CONTEXT --yes      sends SIGTERM to tunnel process
    tunnel-kill-all --yes          sends SIGTERM to all tunnel processes

connect modifies ~/.kube/config (kubeconfig merge). A .bak backup is created
automatically before any write.

---

## Environment variables

    CONFIG_FILE                        override config file path
    K3CTX_CONFIG_DIR                   override config directory
    K3CTX_VERIFY_API_READY             set to 0/false to skip API readiness check
    K3CTX_API_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS    API readiness poll timeout (default 15)

---

## Retry safety

    clients, hosts, status, tunnel-list  — safe to retry, read-only
    connect                              — safe to retry; existing tunnel is reused
    tunnel-kill, tunnel-kill-all         — safe to retry; no-op if already stopped
    init                                 — safe to retry; uses os.MkdirAll

---

## Pagination recipe

    # Page 1
    k3ctx clients --limit 5
    # -> {"ok":true,"data":{"items":[...],"page":{"has_more":true,"next_cursor":"abc"}}}

    # Page 2
    k3ctx clients --limit 5 --cursor abc
